Hey man, sorry to hear you are having problems, I have this occasionally when reading. I find that I concentrate more on reading in the mornings, reading before bed is no good for me. Have you tried meditating? It's really good for focusing the mind on doing 'nothing'. You turn down all the extraneous stimulus until you just have that one idea in your mind. Try it: Get in a comfy position, I prefer to lie down. Take a few deep breaths and relax out your body. Holding tension in your shoulders? Relax. Now, say 'and' as you breathe in and 'one' when you breathe out. Breathe in: 'and' breath out: 'two'. Breathe in 'and', breathe out 'three', breathe in 'and, and breathe out, 'four'. Repeat. After a couple of times through, stop saying it out loud but keep going in your mind. Things pop into your head, push them back out and shut the door. Come back to the numbers and the 'and's. I found it helpful to visualise the numbers; seeing them in my mind kept it busy. Practice, enjoy, don't beat yourself up if you're bad at it at first, everyone is. Practice, get better, learn.

I don't know you exact situation, but I think a lot of this has to do with your attitude towards reading on paper. You automatically get distracted by everything surrounding a text when reading on the internet or on a monitor not full-screen.

The natural distraction of multimedia is almost always present. Even on my tablet I tend to check the time, notifications come in which lead me to shortly interrupting my reading / whatever I'm up to at this moment to look at something else.

You've come to the conclusion that reading on a paper is a problem, and your efforts to increase the number of pages is because you genuinely believe you have developed an inabilty to read longer passages.

My experience with that stuff is when I change my attitude, when I say to myself and make me feel to have fun reading, seeing it as an opportunity to do something completely uninterrupted and dive into the text, that's something that is really fun to me.

I don't think you've ever forgotten how to read properly, you just haven't crossed the barrier to get sucked in by a book anymore up to now. I know it's hard to cross, but that's what you have to re-learn imo. And then you can increase the number of pages to read.
